scope: Unix OSD::SecSleep and OSD::MilliSecSleep return when native usleep is interrupted

native_probe.observed: positive_errno=4 alarm=1 returned=1; milliseconds_errno=4 alarm=1 returned=1; negative_errno=4 alarm=1 returned=1

behavior: Pinned Unix OSD::SecSleep and OSD::MilliSecSleep call usleep with native integer products and ignore its return.
A signal directed to the sleeping thread interrupts either native call and returns early.
Rust NativeSleeper calls usleep on Unix and Sleep on Windows for both units; injected Sleeper implementations retain their Duration callback.
The Windows implementation cross-compiles but was not runtime-tested.
limits: Native signed overflow for large seconds or milliseconds is undefined; parity is claimed only where the native int product is defined.
The negative SecSleep(-1) sample is exploratory pinned-glibc evidence for a useconds_t value outside the POSIX range.
Osd::sec_sleep_with and Osd::milli_sec_sleep_with remain Rust injection surfaces; custom sleepers do not model signals unless they choose to.
